Aggregator (5 board pills, 60 feed rows, retention view 6 boards, pin/unpin toast), Shipper Relations (6-tab layout, 11 seeded incentives, add-account modal creates row, rate-card add present), Claims Master (6-tab layout, File Claim modal creates row → 14 total, 8 prevention checkboxes, watchlist/COI/reserve tables). minor.issue: Only 2 of 5 boards (dat, truckstop) get retention_months attached because brokerage LOAD_BOARDS has ids (convoy, uberfreight, 123loadboard) that don't overlap with BOARD_RETENTION_POLICY ids (direct_edi, spot_rate, smartway, eld). Contract 'each with retention_months where policy exists' is technically satisfied, but the intended overlap is only partial. Consider aligning board ids or adding retention policies for the newer board ids.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Align brokerage LOAD_BOARDS ids with BOARD_RETENTION_POLICY so all 5 boards surface retention_months (or add policies for convoy/uberfreight/123loadboard).
OPTIONAL: Fix Uber Freight board pill contrast — either lighten the base color, add an outline, or force white text when the pill background is near-black.
critical_code_review_comments: claims_master._parse() FIXED: `datetime.fromisoformat('2025-01-01')` returns a tz-naive datetime, which was being subtracted from a tz-aware _now_dt() and crashing /api/claims/insurance/verifications with 500. Fix now forces tz=UTC when tzinfo is None. Same pattern is duplicated across boc3_compliance, load_aggregator retention audit, shipper_relations dashboard — audit those _parse-alike helpers for the same defensiveness.

load_aggregator._all_boards() reuses `LOAD_BOARDS` from routes.brokerage but their ids don't match BOARD_RETENTION_POLICY ids — the retention join is silently partial. Either mirror the ids or add a mapping table.

shipper_relations.create_account uses regex-anchored case-insensitive dedupe on company_name. A shipper called `Acme (v2)` will match `Acme (v2)` literally but a stray leading/trailing space or punctuation variant will NOT trigger the 409. Consider normalizing (strip, collapse whitespace, casefold) before the query.

claims_master.file_claim sets priority=high only when claim_amount_usd >= 5000 — for a broker with $50K+ common claims, a $1200 damage claim to a Fortune-100 shipper still deserves 'high'. Consider factoring shipper tier or historical NPS into the priority pick.
ShipperRelations.jsx is 1342 lines — well above the 700-line file-size guideline. Split into a directory (Tabs/Accounts.jsx, Tabs/Incentives.jsx, Tabs/RateCards.jsx, ...) for maintainability.
ClaimsMaster.jsx is 1169 lines — same file-size concern.

BrokerageAggregatorTab.jsx does not clear the persisted user prefs on unmount, so a leftover exclude_hazmat=true from a testing session filters everything to 0 rows without any visible 'filter is applied' indicator. Add a 'Filters active' banner + 'Clear filters' button.
aggregator/pin endpoint accepts any load_id + board_id combo without validating either exists — a stale pin can accumulate. Consider a soft-verification on pin insert.

The _parse timezone bug is now fixed. If insurance COI ever returns 500 again, first suspect a tz-naive datetime subtraction. Aggregator UI honors persisted per-user prefs — testing agent should reset prefs (POST /api/aggregator/prefs with min_rate_per_mile:0, equipment:[]) if the feed appears empty. All e2e modal flows work: shipper-add, rate-card-add, claims-file, aggregator-pin.
rca of the issue: COI 500 root cause: `_parse('2025-01-01')` used `datetime.fromisoformat(...)` which returns a naive datetime for date-only strings. `list_coi` then computed `(exp - _now_dt()).days` where _now_dt() is tz-aware — Python 3.11 raises TypeError. Reproduction: POST /api/claims/insurance/verifications with expiration_date='2025-01-01' → 200, then GET /api/claims/insurance/verifications → 500. Fix: force tz=UTC in _parse when tzinfo is None. Verified fix via test_insurance_coi_status now passing.
